newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finmin backs new Thai Airways share issue.
newsitem.headline: Finmin backs new Thai Airways share issue.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Thursday he backed a proposal for Thai Airways International Plc to float more new shares to increase private sector participation in its management.
Amnuay said a fresh Thai Airways share issue could be made during his tenure at the ministry.
The government currently owns 93 percent of the carrier.
Thai Airways first went public in 1992 when it offered 100 million new shares to its staff and the public.

The airline has in the past few years considered a proposal to float another 200 million shares but its adviser Phatra Thanakit Plc has told the carrier to delay the move until the Thai stock market recovers.
A fresh public offer will raise Thai Airways' total outstanding shares to 1.6 billion shares from 1.4 billion.
Its shares have mostly been traded below their initial public offered price of 60 baht in the past five years. On Thursday the counter closed 1.25 baht lower at 37.25.
Amnuay said increased private ownership in Thai Airways would help improve its management in an industry where competition is intense.
He said the timing of a new share issue would be dictated by the performance of the Thai stock market.
